events.event: US Consumer Confidence & JOLTS job openings

events.note: Hot PCE = more hike odds = pressure on gold.
Biggest event of the week for gold.

experts.note: Kitco's weekly survey: Wall Street is split (5 up, 4 down, 5 sideways); retail is 57% bullish. Marc Chandler: gold needs to clear $4,400 to matter. James Stanley: the yield problem isn't going away soon. Adam Button: gold may need time to consolidate its run from $2,000 to $5,000.

factors.name: Fed rate outlook
factors.note: Warsh has been hawkish since Jackson Hole and the Sept 16 press conference; markets price roughly 66-69% odds of an October hike.

factors.name: US Treasury yields
factors.note: 10-year near 5.10%, highest since 2007. Rising yields make non-yielding gold less attractive.

factors.name: US dollar
factors.note: Dollar at a two-month high after the strongest business-activity reading in 5+ years.

factors.name: War & geopolitics
factors.note: Trump rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz plan and expects strikes to resume after the midterms. Supportive, but escalation is not immediate and higher oil also feeds rate-hike fears.

factors.name: Physical & central-bank demand
factors.note: Central-bank buying and physical demand have repeatedly defended the $4,200-4,300 zone.

factors.name: Price trend
factors.note: Down 2.2% last week and trading below $4,280 resistance, testing $4,200.

factors.name: Trump / trade policy
factors.note: US-China summit and tariff talk in the background; nothing decisive for gold this weekend.

fed.what: Sept 16 FOMC press conference: signalled stubborn inflation may require further rate increases.

source.title: Federal Reserve: Warsh Jackson Hole remarks

fed.what: Jackson Hole (Aug 28): inflation a bigger concern than a slowing labour market; the Fed may have 'work to do'. Gold fell sharply that day.

plan: A daily close back above $4,280 would neutralise the sell lean. A weak PCE or jobs report, or a sudden Iran escalation, is the main upside risk. A clean break below $4,200 opens room lower.

sources.title: Markets.com: Spot gold falls toward $4,200 (28 Sep)
Al Jazeera Iran war live (26 Sep)
NPR: Trump rejects plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz

summary: Gold opened the week lower, slipping toward the $4,200 support in early Asian trade. The weekend war headline (Trump rejecting Iran's Hormuz plan) did not lift it, because high US yields, a strong dollar and ~2-in-3 odds of an October Fed hike are dominating. A heavy US data week (PCE Wednesday, jobs Friday) can flip this quickly.

trump.what: Rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 7 days; reportedly expects bombing to resume after the midterms.

war.what: Iran's FM Araghchi says only a negotiated settlement can end the deadlock; Tehran has not received an official US position.
Saudi-led coalition intercepted projectiles on Sept 26 as ceasefire talks stalled.
